sections.overall: Welcome back Mercedes Mone! After not being seen in the rankings since the start of the year, her return is a welcome boost to the Women's Division and AEW as a whole. Straight back in at #2, as her rating in January has come down steadily from the 130s between January and now. With Elite Wrestler Ratings, the ratings do not re-set to 100 after 6 weeks of inactivity; they continue to evolve based on the time degradation factor, until they eventually settle at 100. So her entry at number 2 is not indicative of just one match. In Mercedes' case, it feels inevitable that she will reclaim number 1 soon!
sections.mens: There were some strong Men's matches on Dynamite this week. The pick of the bunch was Will Ospreay vs Mark Davis in the Owen Hart Tournament, which main evented. This puts Ospreay at #4 - the highest since his return. MJF vs Rush and Kevin Knight vs Mike Bailey for the World Title and TNT Title, respectively, were also well-received bouts, though neither on the same level as the afore-mentioned main event.
sections.womens: For two weeks in a row, we have been treated to two decent Owen Hart Tournament Women's matches. Mone vs Alex Windsor (7.24) on Dynamite and the main event of Collision, Hazuki vs Persophone (7.13) both delivered. Hopefullt this will lead to more chances down the road for many the talented women in AEW.
sections.menstag: No featured Men's tags this week, so The Young Bucks continue their lead ahead of FTR. WIll the status quo change and the Bucks lose their coveted #1 spot at some point?
sections.womenstag: The feud between Divine Dominion and TayJay appears to be over, with small gains from each team in the title match that opened division. Hopefully this is not the end of the latter's opportunities in AEW, as women's tag teams are sorely needed.
sections.trios: We seem to be having groundhog day with the Trios in AEW - no major standouts this week, with the best involving the Death Riders and STP factions (rated 6.5)
